unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Consider the following assumptions for a sequence $\{S_n\}_{n\in\mathbb N}$ such that $S_n\in\mathcal H_K^*$, for each $n\ge1$. Let $\xrightarrow{d}$ denote convergence in distribution for sequences of random variables.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Standing binder of the arbitrary dual-valued sequence in Theorem4.1. It is not automatically the statistical empirical process and does not carry the CMR sampling hypotheses.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Then, a GP $A\sim GP(m,K)$ is a stochastic process such that for any $n\in\mathbb N$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ in $\mathcal X$, the random vector $(A(x_1),A(x_2),\ldots,A(x_n))$ is distributed as a Gaussian vector with mean $(m(x_1),m(x_2),\ldots,m(x_n))$ and covariance matrix with $ij$-th element $K(x_i,x_j)$, $i,j=1,\ldots,n$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original motivating GP definition. The three theorem statements consume explicit Hilbert-space processes and empirical quadratic forms, so GP integration is not a separate theorem dependency merely because it motivates the paper.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
where $\widetilde Z$ and $\widetilde X$ are independent copies of $Z$ and $X$, respectively,
and let $\Pi$ denote the orthogonal projection operator onto the orthocomplement of $g$ in $L_2(X)$, where $L_2(X)$ is the Hilbert space of square integrable measurable functions of $X$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Two distinct source excerpts: the independent-copy convention in(8), and the L2(X) meaning later on the page. Independent copies mean an independent replication of the joint observation; the statement does not assert independence of Z and X within an observation. The projection uses P_X, not the residual-weighted measure mu.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
We consider the Neyman-orthogonal (infeasible) function-parametric process
\[
R_n(\Pi a)=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Pi a(X_i)\varepsilon(Z_i,\theta_0),\qquad a\in\mathcal H_K,
\]
(20)
where $\Pi a(X_i)$ is defined in (13). This process is infeasible because $\Pi$ and $\theta_0$ are unknown.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Proof route for Theorem4.3 through the true-parameter projected process, not an additional printed theorem or premise. Theorem4.1 is applied to it in the proof; this does not import AssumptionA into the definition of the applied statistic.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Define $\dot G:=E[\dot g'(X,\theta_0)\varepsilon(Z,\theta_0)]$.
Proposition 4.2. Under Assumption B,
\[
\|\widehat R_n(\cdot)-R_n(\Pi\cdot)+G(\cdot,\theta_0)\Gamma^{-1}\dot G\sqrt n(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)\|=o_P(1).
\]
(21)
As a corollary, under $H_0$, $\dot G=0$ and hence, $\|\widehat R_n(\cdot)-R_n(\Pi\cdot)\|=o_P(1)$. This result shows the local robustness under the null and the lack of robustness under the alternative when $\dot G\ne0$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Main-text proposition and explanation clarify the role of the null, but neither is an extra Theorem or a dependency of the process definition. Proposition4.2 is proof machinery for Theorem4.3. The non-null correction is relevant to the unresolved scope of the later bootstrap statement.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: For justification of the bootstrap we use the concept of a.s. consistency, denoted by $\xrightarrow{d}$ a.s., see [21] or Chapter 2.9 in [55].
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: The source cites rather than defines the precise conditional-distribution convergence criterion. Preserve the almost-sure qualifier and record the external-definition limit; this is not an ordinary pathwise limit.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
We consider the local (Pitman) alternatives
\[
H_n(\delta):E[\varepsilon(Z,\theta_0)\mid X]=\frac{\delta(X)}{\sqrt n}\text{ a.s.}
\]
where $\delta(X)$ is a non-zero square integrable measurable function of $X$.
We add some more moment conditions to Assumption B.
Assumption B: (v) $E[\delta^2(X)/\sigma_\varepsilon^2(X)]<\infty$ and $E[K^\perp(X,X)\delta^2(X)]<\infty$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: The local-power addition appears after Theorem4.4 and applies to Proposition4.5, not to the preceding Theorems4.3 and4.4. Local alternatives and B(v) are not imported into their statement graphs.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Let $K$ be a kernel on $\mathcal X$ with RKHS $\mathcal H_K$. Then, for any $n\in\mathbb N$, $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathcal X$ and $c=(c_1,\ldots,c_n)'\in\mathbb R^n$,
\[
\sup_{a\in\mathcal B_K}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nc_ia(x_i)=\left\|\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nc_iK(\cdot,x_i)\right\|_K=\sqrt{c'\mathbb Kc}.
\]
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Lemma3.4 is not an inventoried Theorem. Its final equality has a normalization mismatch when mathbb K is taken with Algorithm1’s entries K(x_i,x_j)/n. Preserve the source formula and flag the mismatch without altering the correctly scaled statistic(14) or theorem statements.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: This section discusses the case where the conditional score $g(X,\theta_0)=E[s(Z,\theta_0)\mid X]$ is nonparametric.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Section5 separately develops the nonparametric-score extension and AssumptionC. It contains no additional Theorem environment and is not silently inserted into the parametric-score assumptions of Theorems4.3/4.4.

source_issues.note: The registered source is the IMS manuscript AOS2401-003R2A0.pdf, marked Submitted to the Annals of Statistics. The source has no publication date on the inspected cover. The main-text discussion ends on shared page20 before the mathematical appendix; only the clipped main text is used.

Theorem4.1 uses the covariance operator on H_K, H_K-orthonormal eigenvectors and sqrt(mu_j). Theorem4.3 uses the Kperp integral operator on L2(mu), eigenvectors orthonormal there, and lambda_j multiplying a Kperp-RKHS inner product. Different normalization means the lambda_j coefficient must not be silently changed to sqrt(lambda_j). RKHS representatives for zero eigenvalues and projection membership are implicit in the source.

Theorem4.3 explicitly assumes H0; Theorem4.4 prints only AssumptionB while referring to the same R_infinity. Proposition4.2 shows an additional parameter-estimation term under alternatives. Preserve the bootstrap statement exactly and flag its intended non-null scope as unresolved; do not add H0 to the original or infer unconditional validity under arbitrary alternatives.

B(iv) requires only a root-n O_P estimator rate, whereas Theorem4.4 asserts almost-sure bootstrap consistency and cites the formal convergence concept externally. The main text does not supply a detailed conditional metric definition or additional pathwise estimator assumptions. This census records the stated strength and does not certify its proof or silently weaken a.s. to in probability.

Algorithm1 defines the raw mathbb K entries as K(X_i,X_j)/n. B(ii) then prints lambda_max(mathbb K)=O_P(n^−1), not O_P(1) and not the projected Gram matrix. Retain the exact condition; for standard fixed nonzero kernels this is substantially restrictive and should be checked before assuming the theorem applies to an example.

For the Algorithm1 Gram scaling, the squared norm of n^−1 sum_i c_i K(.,x_i) equals c-prime mathbb K c/n. Lemma3.4 instead prints sqrt(c-prime mathbb K c) for that norm. This mismatch is confined to the auxiliary original lemma passage; the empirical process uses1/sqrt(n), so the statistic norm identity(14) has the compatible scaling.

The source defines sigma_s² as E[s*s-prime|X], which is a p-by-p matrix for p>1, then calls sigma_s² dF_X a measure and writes kappa_s<infinity without an explicit trace, norm or componentwise convention. Preserve the matrix-valued expression and leave its scalarization unresolved.

Population Gamma is assumed nonsingular and empirical Gamma_n is asserted nonsingular for sufficiently large n. The source gives no convention for singular finite samples. Pi is initially an L2(P_X) projection, the empirical process is indexed by H_K, and the spectral expansion uses L2(mu); these three domains are distinct. No generalized inverse or universal RKHS/L2 isometry is inserted.

Theta is compact and theta0 may be on its boundary, while Theta0 is introduced as a small neighborhood in R^p and differentiability is stated in Theta. The extension/relative-domain convention for derivatives and suprema near a boundary is implicit. Preserve the printed domains without strengthening to an interior parameter or a globally extended function.

B(v) is introduced after Theorem4.4 for local-power Proposition4.5. Section5 separately treats estimated nonparametric conditional scores under AssumptionC. Neither is retroactively added to Theorems4.3/4.4. Proposition4.2 and the application of Theorem4.1 are proof steps, not new assumptions of the applied process definitions.

W_i are iid joint observations, without independence of Z_i and X_i. The weighted measure uses E[epsilon²|X], which equals conditional variance only under conditional mean zero. The multipliers are independent of all original observations, centered, unit variance and bounded; Gaussian multipliers do not satisfy that printed bounded-support assumption.

T4.1.sequence: Arbitrary random S_n in the separable bounded-functional space H_K*, not implicitly a CMR empirical process.
T4.1.assumptions: AssumptionA(i)–(iii), preserving covariance-form positivity, basis summability and the order lim_J limsup_n.
T4.1.limit: S_infinity from the covariance operator T_sigma, sqrt(mu_j), H_K-orthonormal basis and iid standard normals.
T4.1.convergence: Hoffmann-Jorgensen weak convergence in H_K* with its operator norm and Borel sigma field.

T4.3.sampling: Standing iid scalar moment-function model; fitted theta and conditional scores.
T4.3.assumptions: Explicit AssumptionB(i)–(iv) and H0. No B(v), AssumptionC or AssumptionA added as statement premises.
T4.3.local_binders: R_infinity(a) is defined inline by the printed lambda_j<Kperp-inner-product> series; a ranges over H_K and U_j are iid standard normals under page11 convention. That formula is separately archived as D22 for its reuse by Theorem4.4.
T4.3.conclusions: Dual weak convergence and the n*Qhat quadratic statistic limit sum_j lambda_j U_j². Preserve the factor n and L2(mu) eigenbasis.

T4.4.assumptions: AssumptionB(i)–(iv) only in the printed statement; bounded iid centered unit-variance bootstrap multipliers independent of data are standing Section4.3 conditions.
T4.4.limit: R_infinity is a definition reference to the inline formula in Theorem4.3, not an imported H0 premise or theorem-proof invocation.
T4.4.convergence: Almost-sure conditional bootstrap distributional convergence of the scalar squared operator norm. Formal external convergence definition and non-null scope remain explicitly noted.
T4.4.bootstrap: Hold fitted theta, residuals and score projection fixed; resample V_i only.

ambient_conventions: Real Euclidean spaces, conditional expectations, matrix transpose/inverse, Gaussian vectors, orthonormal bases, Hilbert norms and stochastic-order notation are ambient; no mathlib verdict is made.
U_j are iid standard normals under the page11 standing convention. Their appearance in Theorem4.3/4.4 does not require the abstract S_infinity construction or AssumptionA.
Theta-hat is a supplied estimator, with its rate imposed separately by B(iv). The base construction evaluates g(X_i,theta-hat); nonparametric g-hat is a later extension.
All source excerpts are main-text only; assumptions, definitions and proof-only propositions retain their distinct source identities. Source and schema checks do not certify mathematical proofs.
